SYNTHETIC TRAINING NOTE — NOT REAL PATIENT DATA
Note Type: Gastroenterology Consult Note
Author: GI Fellow
Date: 2026-05-08

Reason for Consult: Evaluation of acute abdominal pain in admitted patient.

HPI: 58-year-old admitted today with two days of right lower quadrant pain
and nausea. CT preliminarily reviewed by radiology suggests possible
inflammatory changes adjacent to terminal ileum. No prior history of IBD.

Past Medical History: Hypertension, GERD, prior appendectomy.

Imaging: CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast — radiology preliminary read
notes mild bowel wall thickening of terminal ileum, no free air,
no abscess.

Assessment and Plan: Possible terminal ileitis vs early infectious enteritis.
Recommend continue NPO, IV fluids, repeat labs in AM, consider colonoscopy
if symptoms persist beyond 48 hours. Pain control with short-acting IV
opioid PRN per primary team. GI will follow.
